{"description":"FIX 4 OF GITHUB ISSUE #616. Planned 2026-09-28 under dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id (accepted that day, option (e) with a rule for every exposure). It answers fact:root-cause-an-exposed-server-accepts-any-callers-signature-because-the-boundary-where-write-rules-attach-was-named-and-no-rule-was-chosen-2026-09-28 and fact:collapse-decision-settles-a-decision-with-no-approver-and-says-nothing-2026-09-28.

BEHAVIOUR, from the ruling:
· Local is unchanged: stdio, --shared, loopback --http.
· Exposed (--http-allow-host given) with an OIDC issuer configured: reflow2 is an OAuth 2.0 resource server. It fetches and caches the issuer's JWKS, validates the Bearer JWT (signature, iss, aud, exp; refuses alg none, HS* and any alg that does not fit the key), and may require a claim. It serves /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and answers 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...`. The contributor is derived from a verified claim through an OPERATOR-configured mapping (for example a template like `who:{preferred_username}` plus an optional map file). The mapping is operator config and NOT a Contributor property, because any caller can upsert a Contributor through add_contributor and would otherwise re-point someone else's sign-in. The contributor must already exist; reflow2 never invents the person. Every AUTHORED_BY a call writes, author or approver, must be for that contributor, and anything else is refused.
· Exposed with a declared trusted gateway (flo2's case): writes_for and approver are trusted as given, and the handshake says so.
· Exposed with nothing declared: reads and proposals work, and every SETTLING write is refused with the flags named. Settling means an approver edge, a Requirement status past proposed, a Decision accepted or deferred, a DesignRule `enforced` set, or a VIOLATES_RULE status set (tools/check_intent_authority.py settles_intent).

WHERE IT IS ENFORCED, so no write path can bypass it (mapped 2026-09-28 at HEAD da4a12b):
1. TRANSPORT: one tower wrapper in main.rs serve_http, right after `make(config)` next to the Host gate from fix 1 (host_gate.rs). It covers the single-design, shared, ephemeral, degraded and registry servers, and stdio never passes it. It verifies the token and puts a `Caller` (verified contributor, gateway, or undeclared) into req.extensions_mut(). rmcp carries http::request::Parts and extensions into RequestContext.extensions.
2. SERVICE: service.rs call_tool takes the author from the Caller, not from _meta or the session. write_lock, the only way to get the graph for writing, installs the policy on the DesignGraph for the life of the GraphWrite and clears it on drop, as the touch log does. credit_writes runs on drop, so the policy must allow the verified caller's own author edge.
3. CORE: graph.rs create_edge (every AUTHORED_BY and VIOLATES_RULE status passes it: typed door, the generic create_edge tools, import, merge), plus create_node and create_node_refs_checked_later (every Requirement or Decision status and DesignRule `enforced`), comparing stored against new. Multi-step handlers such as add_requirement pre-check through refuse_settling_without_approver (capture.rs), so a refusal leaves no half-write. Decide whether delete_edge on an approver edge ("unsigning") is also guarded.

FLO2 COUPLING: flo2's reflow2 container is exposed. The reflow2 release carrying this must ship with flo2 declaring the trusted gateway, in the same upgrade, or flo2's approvals are refused. Record this in flo2's design when the flag name is final.

OPEN SUB-CHOICES, the agent's to propose at build time and not the owner's word yet: the flag names (for example --http-oidc-issuer, --http-oidc-audience, --http-oidc-required-claim, --http-contributor-id, --http-trust-gateway, --http-public-url); whether ring is used directly for RS256/ES256 or a vetted JWT crate is added (ring 0.17 and base64 are transitive only; there is no JWT or JWK code in the tree; mcp_http.rs's TLS client is POST-only JSON-RPC, so a JWKS GET sibling is needed); and whether the image's "NO AUTHENTICATION" label is rewritten here or in #617.","name":"A server deliberately exposed to other machines establishes who is calling (a verified token, or a declared trusted gateway) before anyone can settle intent, and refuses settling when neither is declared","provenance":"authored","status":"planned","tier":"operational"}
